guide.a.how_checkin_works:
Each ticket has its own QR code — the square barcode you scan with a phone. When an attendee arrives, they show their QR code to a member of staff. The staff member scans it (or opens the link), which opens the check-in page. If signed in as an admin, they see the attendee's details and ticket quantity, with a button to check them in or out.

A booking can hold more than one ticket. When it does, the staff member chooses how many tickets to check in, so part of a group can arrive first. The attendee list offers the same choice, and check-out can also release just some of the tickets.

Check-in works per listing. If an attendee is booked on several listings, checking them in at one does not change their status at the others.
guide.a.qr_code_purpose: The QR code links to the ticket's check-in page. Scanning it opens the page in a browser. Visitors who are not signed in see a message telling them to show the code to staff. Signed-in admins see the attendee's details and a check-in button.
guide.q.use_qr_scanner: How do I use the QR scanner?
guide.a.use_qr_scanner:
Open a listing and click Scanner. Tap Start Camera to begin — the first time, your phone asks permission to use the camera. Point the camera at an attendee's QR code and they are checked in automatically. The scanner works best with the back camera on a phone.

To check people in for a whole group, open the group and click Scanner. One scan checks in one listing at a time. To make one scan check in every listing the ticket holds, open the group's Edit form and tick Check in every listing in this group when scanning any. With it ticked, the scanner page warns that one scan checks in every listing.
guide.q.scanner_no_checkout: Why doesn't the scanner check people out?
guide.a.scanner_no_checkout: The scanner only checks people in, never out. This stops a double-scan at a busy door from accidentally checking someone out. To check someone out, use their ticket's own check-in page.
guide.q.qr_different_listing: What if a QR code is for a different listing?
guide.a.qr_different_listing: The scanner looks at all the attendee's listings. If they are booked on the listing you are scanning, check-in proceeds normally. If they are only booked on other listings, you are asked to confirm before checking them in. This lets you handle last-minute listing changes without turning anyone away.
guide.q.scanner_status_messages: What do the scanner status messages mean?
guide.a.scanner_status_messages: Checked in — shows the attendee's name and ticket count (for example "Jo checked in (2 tickets)"). When the booking holds more tickets than were checked in, the count names both (for example "Jo checked in (2 of 3 tickets)"). How many tickets — the booking holds more than one ticket, so the scanner asks how many people are present before it checks them in. Already checked in — every ticket on the booking was already checked in. Refunded — the attendee has been refunded and cannot be checked in. Ticket not found — the QR code does not match any booking. Different listing — a confirmation box asks whether to check them in anyway. ID verification — for non-transferable listings, staff are asked to confirm the attendee's ID matches the ticket name before check-in.
guide.a.what_is_apple_wallet: Apple Wallet is the app on iPhones that holds tickets and cards. When set up, attendees see an Add to Apple Wallet button on their ticket page. Tapping it saves the ticket to their iPhone and Apple Watch. The pass shows the listing name, date, location, ticket quantity, price paid, and a QR code for check-in.
guide.q.setup_apple_wallet: How do I set up Apple Wallet?
guide.wallet_setup.apple_note: This set-up needs an Apple Developer account, which costs about $99 a year. Most people ask their web builder to do this part.
guide.wallet_setup.google_note: This set-up needs a Google Cloud account. Most people ask their web builder to do this part.
guide.q.wallet_passes_update: Do Apple Wallet tickets update themselves?
guide.a.wallet_passes_update: Yes. Apple Wallet checks with this site about once a day and refreshes the ticket with the latest details. Attendees can also pull down on the ticket in the Wallet app to refresh it right away.
guide.q.do_google_wallet_passes_update_a: Do Google Wallet tickets update themselves?
guide.a.do_google_wallet_passes_update_a: No. Google Wallet tickets are a one-time copy made when the attendee adds them. If listing details change later, the ticket in their wallet stays as it was. The attendee can remove and re-add it from their ticket page to get the latest details.
guide.q.what_if_someone_doesn_t_have_the: What if someone doesn't have their QR code?
guide.a.what_if_someone_doesn_t_have_the: Below the camera on the Scanner page there is a Manual Check-in section. Start typing the attendee's name and a list shows matching tickets that have not been checked in yet. Select the right person and click Check In. This is useful for walk-ins, or when someone cannot pull their ticket up on their phone.
guide.q.how_do_i_filter_attendees_by_che: How do I filter attendees by check-in status?
guide.a.how_do_i_filter_attendees_by_che:
On the listing page, above the attendee table, you will see filter links for All, Checked In, and Checked Out. Click one to show only attendees with that status.

The filter works with the date picker for daily listings, so you can view, for example, only the not-yet-checked-in attendees for one date. The CSV export follows whichever filter is on.
guide.a.what_is_google_wallet_integratio: Google Wallet is the app on Android phones that holds tickets and cards. When set up, attendees see an Add to Google Wallet button on their ticket page. Tapping it saves the ticket to their Google Wallet. The pass shows the listing name, date, location, ticket quantity, price paid, and a QR code for check-in.
